title: Schedule Footnote: the Share the Length of the Journey Carries — Travel Protection Plans
content:
The destination loading owed on a Travel Protection Plans certificate is taken at a share of the plan's destination loading percentage which the length of the journey insured carries. The length of the journey insured is counted in whole calendar days from the first day of the journey to its last day, both days counted.

Where the journey insured runs for more than half the plan's longest single journey and the certificate declares a region other than domestic, the share the length of the journey insured carries is the whole of the plan's destination loading percentage, that is 100 per cent of it.

Where the journey insured runs for half the plan's longest single journey or less and the certificate declares a region other than domestic, the share the length of the journey insured carries is 70 per cent.

Where neither holds, the share the length of the journey insured carries is 40 per cent, because a journey wholly within the country of residence carries the least exposure to a foreign risk.

## The plan's longest single journey, against which the half is measured

| Plan | Longest single journey, days | Half of it, days |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Trip Basics Essential | 30 | 15 |
| Trip Basics Standard | 45 | 22.5 |
| TripGuard Plus | 60 | 30 |
| TripGuard Premier | 90 | 45 |
| Cancel For Any Reason Elite | 90 | 45 |
| Annual Multi-Trip Traveller | 30 | 15 |
| Annual Multi-Trip Executive | 60 | 30 |

## Both sides of the threshold

On a plan whose longest single journey is 60 days, half of it is 30 days.

- A journey insured of 31 whole days, on a certificate declaring a region other than domestic, runs for more than half the plan's longest single journey, so the share is 100 per cent.
- A journey insured of exactly 30 whole days, on a certificate declaring a region other than domestic, runs for half the plan's longest single journey and no more, so the share is 70 per cent.
- A journey insured of 31 whole days on a certificate declaring the domestic region reaches neither of those, so the share is 40 per cent, as does a journey of 30 days or fewer on such a certificate.

Counting the days: a journey whose first day is the 4th of a month and whose last day is the 10th of that month runs 7 whole days, both the first day and the last day being counted.
